title: Tax on $120k Salary Australia: What You Actually Take Home After Tax and Super

faqs.q: What is the tax on $120,000 salary in Australia for 2026-27?
faqs.a: For the 2026-27 income year, a resident earning $120,000 pays $26,520 in income tax plus a 2% Medicare levy ($2,400), for total deductions of $28,920. That leaves a net annual income of $91,080. The tax is calculated using the resident tax-free threshold ($18,200), then 15% on the next $26,800, and 30% on the remaining $75,000.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52. For a standard full-time role of 38 hours per week, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. For example, $60.73 per hour gives $60.73 × 38 × 52 = $120,000. If you work different hours, adjust the weekly figure accordingly. Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) page explains this in more detail.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding the Tax on $120k Salary Australia

If you earn $120,000 a year, you’re well above the national average and likely working full-time. But what does that figure actually mean for your weekly, fortnightly, and annual take-home pay? This guide breaks down the tax on 120k salary Australia using the latest 2026-27 rates, explains how to convert your hourly rate, and shows what you can expect after the Medicare levy and super guarantee.

### Converting Your Hourly Rate to an Annual Salary

The standard formula for full-time work is:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

Most full-time employees work 38 hours a week under a modern award or the National Employment Standards. So a $120,000 salary implies an hourly rate of about $60.73 ($120,000 ÷ (38 × 52)). If you’re paid a different hourly rate, you can use the same formula in reverse. Our [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) tool helps you move between hourly, weekly, and annual figures.

Remember that this calculation assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. It also assumes you’re a permanent employee – casual workers receive a 25% loading on top of the base rate, which would increase the annual equivalent.

### Tax on $120,000: The 2026-27 Resident Scale

The Australian Taxation Office applies a progressive tax system. For the 2026-27 income year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

On $120,000, your tax is calculated as:

- $0 on the first $18,200
- 15% on $26,800 ($18,201 to $45,000) = $4,020
- 30% on $75,000 ($45,001 to $120,000) = $22,500
- **Total income tax = $26,520**

### The Medicare Levy

Most residents also pay the Medicare levy, which is 2% of your taxable income. For a $120,000 salary, that’s an additional $2,400. The levy helps fund Australia’s public healthcare system. If you’re on a lower income you may be eligible for a reduction, but at this income level the full 2% applies.

**Total deductions (tax + Medicare) = $28,920**

**Net annual income = $120,000 – $28,920 = $91,080**

### Fortnightly and Weekly Take-Home Pay

If you’re paid fortnightly, divide the net annual figure by 26. For $91,080, that’s about $3,503 per fortnight. Weekly, it’s about $1,752. These figures are after tax and Medicare but before any salary sacrifice, HELP repayments, or the Medicare levy surcharge (which applies if you don’t have private hospital cover and earn above a threshold).

### Super Guarantee: Paid on Top

Your $120,000 salary is your base pay. Under the super guarantee, your employer must contribute an additional 12% of your ordinary earnings into a super fund, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. That means an extra $14,400 per year, bringing your total employment cost to $134,400. This super is not part of your take-home pay – it’s invested for your retirement. You can learn more about how super interacts with your salary on our [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) page.

### Casual Loading and Award Rates

If you’re a casual employee, you’re entitled to a 25% loading on the base hourly rate. For a permanent employee earning $60.73 per hour, the casual equivalent would be $75.91 per hour. That would push the annual equivalent (if you worked the same hours) to $150,000 – but casual work often involves irregular hours. Always check your award or enterprise agreement for the correct classification. The Fair Work Ombudsman publishes [pay guides](/blog) with minimum rates for each award.

### Comparing to National Benchmarks

The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. A $120,000 salary is well above that. The Australian Bureau of Statistics reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 in May 2026, which equates to about $108,352 per year. So $120,000 is roughly 11% above the average full-time salary.

### Important Caveats

This estimate uses the 2026-27 resident tax scale and the standard 2% Medicare levy. It does not account for:

- The Medicare levy surcharge (if you don’t have appropriate private hospital cover)
- HELP or other study loan repayments
- Salary sacrifice arrangements
- Pre-tax deductions like workplace giving
- State payroll tax or other employer obligations

For a personalised calculation, use our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) tool or consult the ATO’s tax withheld calculator. Remember that your actual pay may differ if you work overtime, receive allowances, or have a different work pattern.

### Summary

A $120,000 annual salary translates to about $60.73 per hour for a 38-hour week. After income tax of $26,520 and the Medicare levy of $2,400, your net annual income is $91,080 – or $3,503 per fortnight. Your employer also pays $14,400 in super on top. Understanding the tax on 120k salary Australia helps you budget, negotiate, and plan for the future.
